races.name: Anglo Stainless Supporting Yorkshire Wooden Spoon Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Trojan Soldier
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who finally won in cheekpieces at Southwell but faces a 40-day layoff and needs pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Stays 2m and he's a player if transferring this year's AW improvement back to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in four of his first five handicaps before finally cracking it in a four-runner race at Southwell (1m6f, AW) in April; that was in first-time cheekpieces (retained) but by just a nose, leading on the post; stays 2m and he's a player if transferring this year's improvement back to turf.

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner in excellent form with a Bath win and C&D second, perfectly suited to control this race
runners_data.comment: Ready winner at Bath (2m1f) and good second over C&D (good) eight days later; player
runners_data.spotlight: Ready winner at Bath (2m1f, good to firm) on reappearance and good second under Mason Paetel over C&D (good) eight days later; another bold bid looks on its way.

runners_data.name: Vaguely Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing improvement with third at Southwell but lacks a Flat win since 2022
runners_data.comment: Has another career-low mark but it's hard to know when he will take advantage
runners_data.spotlight: There was some restoration of his Flat fortunes when third of five at Southwell (1m6f, AW; stays 2m) on latest start but he's without a win on the Flat since the end of 2023; has another career-low mark but it's hard to know when he will take advantage.

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up performer with excellent 2025 record including course runner-up, needs genuine pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Had a good 2025; this year's return was downbeat affair behind Scottish Dancer 15 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Had a good 2025, winning over 1m7f at Ayr (good to firm) and 2m at Chester (good); also runner-up on five occasions, including here (short-headed) and on his reappearance, but this year's return was a downbeat affair behind Scottish Dancer 15 days ago.

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse facing a 72-day break and poor recent form, needs everything to fall perfectly

runners_data.name: Rupert The Prince
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with 13lb weight advantage but struggling over hurdles this year, unknown current form level
runners_data.comment: Fair third over C&D on his only Flat run this year and peak form gives him a good shout
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times (once from rear, twice making all) at up to 2m last term on the Flat for Paddy Butler; remote this year in his two hurdle races (three-runner race last time) but he was a fair third over C&D (a head behind No More Bolero) in between and peak form gives him a good shout.

runners_data.name: Scottish Dancer
runners_data.note: Won on front-running return to Flat after hurdle struggles, but faces quick turnaround and stronger opposition
runners_data.comment: 33-1 outsider of five for Thirsk 1m6f win; back up just 2lb and return to 2m may well suit
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way in Ireland last year as a hurdler but, having first Flat run since June 2023, made a winning start from the front for new yard in handicap at Thirsk (1m6f, good to firm) 15 days ago; the big outsider of five that day and dictated a slow pace, but he's gone back up by just 2lb and the return to 2m may well suit him; major player in bid to win a second time under Millie Wonnacott.

races.paceDynamic: No More Bolero will dictate from the front with Rupert The Prince likely to race prominently in second, creating a sustainable but genuine gallop over this stamina-testing 2m trip. With only two natural pace-setters and five hold-up horses, the early fractions should be manageable before quickening from 4f out. The lack of pace pressure early means front-runners can conserve energy for a strong finish, while hold-up horses face the risk of the race not falling apart late. This shape clearly favours prominent racers and the early pace-setters who can control their own destiny.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If No More Bolero gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: The 7-year-old can use his tactical speed to quicken when it matters, making it hard for hold-up horses to close down in time. His recent Bath win and C&D second under these exact conditions make him perfectly suited to exploit this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow early allowing hold-up horses to close effectively
scenarios.body: Marbuzet's proven course form and Scottish Dancer's front-running return to form give them the tactical speed to pounce when the race opens up. The stamina-laden nature of this contest could see hold-up horses with the best recent form surge late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rupert The Prince can stalk the pace perfectly and time his challenge
scenarios.body: Despite his hurdle struggles this year, his three Flat wins last season all came at distances up to 2m with prominent tactics. A 13lb weight advantage and claimer's allowance make him dangerous if finding his old form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If both pace-setters go too fast early and completely capitulate
scenarios.body: The race would become a sitting duck for the best hold-up performer with tactical speed. Trojan Soldier's recent Southwell win in cheekpieces shows he has the ability when everything falls right.

watchPoints.text: No More Bolero's early position - if he gets an uncontested lead the race could be over before the turn
Scottish Dancer's jumping from the front - any early mistakes or hesitation could compromise his prominent position
Trojan Soldier's headgear - if the cheekpieces aren't applied it removes his key form angle
Rupert The Prince's settling - needs to track the pace rather than fight for the lead to be effective
The pace through the first mile - if too slow it opens the door for all the hold-up horses

runners_data.name: Tricky Jenny

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs a strong pace to be effective but race may not develop to suit her style

runners_data.name: Crimson Blaze
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter who can control the race but has shown concerning hanging tendencies on artificial surfaces
runners_data.comment: Hung left on both starts, including when favourite latest; can do better at some point
runners_data.spotlight: She hasn't lived up to her market billing in two 5f runs on AW, hanging left on debut and again at Southwell 18 days ago when Oisin Murphy allowed her to come home in her own time once her chance had gone; should do better at some point and at least she'll have a rail to help if she hangs today.

races.paceDynamic: Crimson Blaze will lead unchallenged from the gates with The Can Can Queen, Fern Clyde and Tricky Jenny settling prominently behind her. The early pace will be steady rather than fierce, allowing the field to remain compact through halfway. With limited early speed in the field, this sets up perfectly for horses that can quicken from prominent positions or those with a turn of foot from midfield. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close enough to strike.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Crimson Blaze gets an easy lead and finds her rhythm
scenarios.body: She can dictate terms throughout and prove hard to peg back despite her recent disappointing efforts. The tactical advantage of controlling the pace from the front will outweigh any stamina concerns over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can sit perfectly positioned behind Crimson Blaze
scenarios.body: The Can Can Queen or Fern Clyde can use their tactical speed to challenge turning for home when the leader comes under pressure. Their racing experience gives them the edge over the lightly-raced runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace allows Eevee Star or Bai Tong to show their true ability
scenarios.body: Either can make significant improvement from their debuts and benefit from the tactical race setup. The undemanding early gallop will help them settle and showcase any latent ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes crawling and Cheeky Chesca gets the perfect run
scenarios.body: She can use her hold-up style to devastating effect with a well-timed late challenge. The lack of early pace will compress the field and create opportunities for closing runners.

watchPoints.text: Crimson Blaze hanging left again under pressure could compromise her chance and affect others
The Can Can Queen and Fern Clyde both need to be positioned close enough to strike when the pace lifts
Bai Tong's market support will indicate connections' confidence after her disappointing debut effort
Spirit Of Mary's tendency to fade means she needs to be produced late to have any chance
Eevee Star's early positioning will reveal her preferred running style and tactical intentions

races.paceDynamic: Popeye Doyle and Poet's Dawn appear to be the only prominent runners, with Spirit Catcher also capable of taking a forward position early. The majority field is comprised of hold-up horses who need the race to develop, creating a scenario where the early leaders won't face genuine pressure through the opening stages. This will likely produce a moderate tempo that suits those who can track the pace and have a finishing kick. The abundance of hold-up horses and lack of genuine pace pressure strongly favours horses who can sit prominent or just off the lead, rather than those coming from the back of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Popeye Doyle and Poet's Dawn set a steady tempo without pressure from behind.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows prominent runners and those tracking to position perfectly for a sustained finish. Hold-up horses from the rear struggle to make up the ground as the leaders haven't come back to them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Finish From Held-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the field bunches entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The compressed field gives the strong finishers from the back their optimal scenario to unleash late runs. Horses with proven finishing kicks can sweep past those who went too early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runners Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If Popeye Doyle or Poet's Dawn improve dramatically and the pace becomes genuinely searching.
scenarios.body: The honest early gallop stretches the field and exposes those without the stamina for the trip. The leaders maintain their advantage as the hold-up horses fail to close the gap.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish from halfway.
scenarios.body: The stop-start nature catches many horses flat-footed and allows unconsidered runners with tactical speed to strike. Form lines become less reliable in a messy tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Popeye Doyle could lead throughout if his two AW wins translate to turf and the pace stays moderate
Watch for market support for Finlaggan who showed dramatic improvement when stepped up in trip last time
Spirit Catcher needs to prove his Musselburgh win wasn't just a product of a weak contest
Any significant drift in the market about Poet's Dawn given his age and recent moderate form
Monitor early positioning of the hold-up horses as track position will be crucial in a large field

runners_data.name: Lebron Power
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with inconsistent recent form but tactical positioning could prove crucial

races.paceDynamic: Shallow provides the only confirmed front-running presence in this 9-runner field, setting up a sustainable early pace without immediate pressure from the start. Beaujolais Nouveau, Saffron Dandy and Lebron Power will likely track just behind in prominent positions, but none are natural speed horses who will challenge Shallow's early supremacy. The large contingent of hold-up runners (Powdering, Alpine Girl, Anaisa, Cotai Belle, Space Bear) will sit towards the back, creating a compressed field behind a solid but uncontested pace. This race shape heavily favours the prominent runners who can position themselves within striking distance without getting caught up in a late traffic jam.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners secure good positions behind Shallow's honest pace
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get caught in traffic as prominent runners have clear runs to challenge from ideal positions. Beaujolais Nouveau, Saffron Dandy and Lebron Power benefit from tactical positioning without being asked to make the running.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly unsustainable or the field spreads out more than expected
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses find clear passages and their superior finishing kicks prove decisive in the final furlong. Space Bear and Alpine Girl benefit from their proven finishing ability when getting racing room.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Shallow gets an uncontested lead and the field fails to organize an effective challenge
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows Shallow to dictate terms completely and hold off late challengers. Her honest galloping style and proven ability at the trip becomes crucial when controlling the tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Shallow early or the pace becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly messy pace scenario creates opportunities for horses with tactical speed to capitalize on positioning errors. The race becomes more about who adapts best to changing circumstances than natural running styles.

watchPoints.text: Shallow must maintain honest gallop early - if she goes too fast or too slow it changes everything for the prominent runners
Traffic developing in final 2f as multiple hold-up horses (Powdering, Alpine Girl, Anaisa, Space Bear) seek racing room simultaneously
Beaujolais Nouveau and Saffron Dandy securing ideal tracking positions behind Shallow in the first two furlongs
Space Bear's ability to reproduce Yarmouth form stepping up significantly in class against these rivals
Weather conditions remaining stable as any track deterioration would impact the hold-up horses' effectiveness

races.paceDynamic: Quirke On Parole is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead uncontested, setting a controlled gallop that may be too steady for this competitive handicap field. Daring Leader and Penny Ghent could press forward if needed, but the majority are hold-up horses including Barleybrown, Volenti, Little Ted, Oilisa, I Can Boogy, Balqaa, Ring Of Gold, Woodleigh, Far Ahead, Haaf A Diamond, and Arranmore. With 11 of 14 runners preferring to come from behind, the race will develop into a sprint finish where those getting first run from midfield will have a significant advantage over those held up too long. This race shape strongly favours prominent/midfield runners who can position close enough to strike early in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Quirke On Parole maintains a steady gallop without pressure from behind
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader can dictate terms and prove hard to peg back, while any horse tracking close behind gets first run on the field. Daring Leader and Penny Ghent benefit from forward positions while the massed ranks of hold-up horses struggle to make up ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Strike Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and allows midfield runners to position perfectly
scenarios.body: Horses like Woodleigh and Oilisa can get into ideal spots three-four lengths off the leader and time their runs to perfection. The hold-up brigade gets caught too far back as the race becomes a sprint from the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Cavalry Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses completely and becomes a crawl
scenarios.body: The race turns into a 2f dash where the strongest finishers from the back can unleash devastating late runs. Barleybrown and Volenti can overcome their poor positions if they have enough track left to work with.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Quirke On Parole goes too slow early then multiple horses make premature moves
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair with several runners making their effort together from the 3f pole, favouring those with natural pace. I Can Boogy and Balqaa can benefit if they get clear runs in the scramble.

watchPoints.text: Quirke On Parole must handle the pressure of leading throughout and could fold if challenged early by Daring Leader or Penny Ghent

Woodleigh and Oilisa both return from modest efforts but have winning form at this level and could benefit from the likely strong pace
First-time cheekpieces on Haaf A Diamond worked well last time but she faces much stiffer competition here
Watch the market move on I Can Boogy who gets valuable weight relief from the 3lb claimer and showed promise when second two starts ago

races.paceDynamic: Ellie's de Vega is the lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate proceedings from the gate, likely getting an uncontested lead with Simba's Pride (prominent) and Peggy Boo (prominent) tracking behind. The large contingent of hold-up horses (Pivotal Terms, Vega's Virtue, Gunalt Wavelength, Hares Bredth, Tenor's Inn, What A Tahoo) will be bunched at the back, creating a distinct early split. With minimal early pace pressure, Ellie's de Vega can control fractions and kick for home, while the prominent runners get first run on the hold-up brigade. This tactical setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable late traffic problems that will engulf the back-markers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If Ellie's de Vega gets easy fractions with no early pressure from the prominent duo
scenarios.body: She can dictate ideal splits and kick clear in the straight before the hold-up horses get organized. The sheer weight of numbers behind creates inevitable interference and traffic issues.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Takeover
scenarios.trigger: If Simba's Pride or Peggy Boo press Ellie's de Vega early and establish better position
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get first run while the leader tires, but still finish ahead of the trailing pack who face traffic. Superior class of Simba's Pride tells in a speed battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and the field comes back to the hold-up horses
scenarios.body: The back-markers get clear runs and superior finishing speed overcomes positional disadvantage. Pivotal Terms' recent form and Gunalt Wavelength's consistency become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Ellie's de Vega goes too slow early and multiple horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: A blanket finish develops where any horse with a clear passage can win. The 52-day absences of Tenor's Inn and What A Tahoo become less relevant in a sprint finish.

races.paceDynamic: I'm Dan Dare is the sole confirmed front runner and will lead from the gates with Maynora and Luck Money sitting prominent behind him. With limited early pace pressure, I'm Dan Dare can dictate a controlled tempo through the opening furlongs before the field fans out. The lack of multiple pace pressers means this will develop into a tactical affair where positioning becomes crucial. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can sit close to the pace and kick when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Dan Dare gets an uncontested lead and sets moderate fractions
scenarios.body: The lone leader can measure out his effort perfectly while prominent runners like Maynora get ideal positioning to strike. Hold-up horses will find themselves too far back when the pace quickens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and multiple horses bunch up behind the leader
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where tactical speed and positioning trump stamina, suiting those who can travel well in behind. Horses with finishing kicks will benefit from the shorter sustained effort required.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Dan Dare goes too fast early or the prominent runners engage in a pace battle
scenarios.body: The early pace collapses allowing closers to sweep up from the back as the leaders tire. This scenario requires genuine pace pressure up front to set it up properly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites underperform due to track position or traffic problems
scenarios.body: Horses with less exposed form or significant weight advantages can capitalize on a messy race where class doesn't tell. The handicap nature allows for surprise packages to emerge.
